info.title: ORBIT API
info.description:
Open Agent Platform control plane API.

Authentication is bearer-token based: an OIDC access token, an ORBIT API key (`orbit_sk_…`), or the development token depending on ORBIT_AUTH_MODE. The same API serves the web app and future native mobile clients.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
`draft`, `active`, `paused`, `archived`, or `current` for every agent that is
not archived.

parameters.name: hard
parameters.description: Permanently delete the agent and its execution history (default: archive).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One execution status, or several separated by commas (`failed,timed_out`).

parameters.description: Only approvals requested by this execution.

502.description: The identity provider's discovery document could not be read

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for tokens. The client secret stays on the server.

502.description: The identity provider rejected or failed the exchange

get.summary: Documentation index: categories and their pages.

200.description: Categories and pages (JSON), or an HTML index with `format=html`

get.summary: One documentation page, or an embedded asset when the path starts with `assets/`.
get.description:
A single route serves both so that a page slug such as `assets/brand` and the
asset tree cannot shadow each other: an exact asset match wins, otherwise the path
is looked up as a page slug. The `{*path}` catch-all matches nested slugs; keep the
annotation in sync with the route in `routes.rs`.

parameters.name: *path
parameters.description: Page slug (e.g. `architecture/overview`) or asset path under `assets/...`

200.description: A page as metadata and Markdown (JSON), raw Markdown (`format=markdown`) or HTML (`format=html` / `Accept: text/html`); or the asset bytes with their content type

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One execution status, or several separated by commas (`failed,timed_out`).

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of a tool, capability, connector or connection identifier.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the event message or tool/action identifiers.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream: snapshot, replay of persisted events, then tail.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: agents, skills, connections, providers, worker_profiles, agent_teams, triggers or tool_policies

200.description: Secret-free resource export (JSON, portable YAML or SKILL.md)

parameters.description: `create` (default: a name conflict is a 409), `update` or `upsert`.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report only; nothing is written.

requestBody.description: SKILL.md, a YAML/JSON portable document, or a multi-document bundle. May be wrapped as {"content", "filename"} JSON.

200.description: Dry-run report, or an import that only updated resources

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many deliveries to return, newest first (1–200, default 50).

post.summary: Probe an unsaved provider config (create dialog).
Probe an OpenAI-compatible endpoint by listing models.

put.description:
This is a merge: only the fields present in `settings` change, and absent fields
(including `roleClaim`, `groupRoles`, `teamGroups`, `autoCreateTeams`,
`requireMappedGroup` and `syncRoles`) are preserved. To clear a mapping, send it
explicitly (for example `"groupRoles": {}`). The merged result is validated before
it is stored.

patch.summary: Bulk visibility/ownership update for agents, skills and other shareable resources.
patch.description:
Partial success is intentional: one resource the caller cannot manage must not block
the rest, and the response says exactly which ids failed.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Only runs of this agent team.

get.summary:
Access overview for one access team. The whole page (summary + first page of resources)
is one request; every resource is filtered by the caller's `AccessScope` before it is
returned, so a team member never sees another team's resources through this endpoint.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Include agent rules and org defaults

teamIsolation.description: Non-admins only see resources owned by their access teams.

AgentDefinition.description:
Portable, versioned agent definition (`orbit.io/v1`).

This is the import/export format. It is validated before persistence; the API
accepts and returns it, and `agent_versions.spec` stores the inner `AgentSpec`.

consecutiveFailures.description: Failed executions in a row; reset when an execution succeeds.

failedExecutionId.description: Last failed execution already counted and backed off from.

oneOf.description:
Deprecated compatibility field. New agent versions omit it; runtime selection is
per execution/trigger/team step.

harnessConfig.description: Harness-specific options keyed by harness kind (`opencode`, `pi`, …).

runDefaults.description: Defaults used when a manual run is created without an explicit task.

skills.description: Slugs from the organization's skill library to materialize in the workspace.
Slugs of the skills in the current version, so a skill can show which agents use it.

approvalsRequireDifferentApprover.description:
Four-eyes: the user who requested an execution cannot approve or reject the
approvals that execution raises. Default `false`.

code.description:
Stable envelope code from the equivalent single-resource request (`forbidden`,
`not_found`, `conflict`, `bad_request`).

dryRun.description:
Evaluate eligibility and report results without changing anything. Used by the web
UI to explain mixed selections before asking for confirmation.

deleted.description: Ids deleted by this request (empty for archive requests).

unchanged.description: Ids already in the requested state; no change was made.

updated.description: Ids archived by this request (empty for delete requests).

clearOwnerTeam.description: Explicitly clear the owning team when no ownerTeamId is sent.

supported.description:
False when ORBIT has no probe for this connector. Nothing was contacted and
the connection's status is left as it was.

ConnectorBinding.description:
A connector reference. The shorthand string form (`- gitlab`) parses to a binding
without a connection, but semantic validation rejects it: a usable connector binding
must name the concrete connection that supplies its credentials and access scope.

capabilities.description:
Explicit capability allowlist (`issues.list`, `messages.send`, …).
Empty means "manifest default read capabilities only" (never write).

credential.description: Raw credential (API token, bot token, …). Encrypted at rest.

harness.description: Harness for this execution. `harnessOverride` is accepted as a legacy alias.

placement.description:
Where this run may execute: `auto` (any matching worker), `local`, `docker` or
`kubernetes`. Overrides the placement stored on the agent for this run only.

skills.description: Skills to materialize for this execution, in addition to the agent spec.

task.description: The task or message for the agent.

credential.description: Raw credential, encrypted at rest. Never returned by the API.

branch.description: Optional base/working branch for repository checkout.

harness.description: Harness for team steps. Falls back to the legacy agent harness or org default.

instructions.description:
Shared goal/instruction for the team. Passed to every step as configured system
context, never mixed into the run instruction shown as the task.

mode.description:
`pipeline` runs each agent once in order. `native` runs the primary agent only
and materializes the remaining agents as harness-native subagents.

repositories.description: Multi-repository workspace. When empty, `repository`/`branch` are used.

repository.description:
Structured workspace repository (owner/repo). Instructions alone cannot drive
repository checkout; this is passed to the worker.

skills.description: Skills materialized for every step in the team.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-step wall-clock timeout; defaults to 1 hour for team runs.

workerProfileId.description: Worker profile used for automatic launch.

autoApprove.description: Explicitly allow bound writes for this run without per-call approvals (L4).

harnessOverride.description: Override the agent's stored harness for this run.

task.description: Optional run-specific task. Falls back to the team instruction.

harness.description: Optional harness for executions fired by this trigger.

agentScope.description: `all` (dynamic) or `selected`; omitted derives from agentIds for compatibility.

allowWebFetch.description: Allow OpenCode's built-in WebFetch tool. Default false for headless runs.

allowWebSearch.description: Allow OpenCode's built-in Web Search tool. Default false for headless runs.

env.description:
Variable name -> value. A string sets or replaces the value; `null` keeps the
stored value (422 when none is stored); a name left out is removed. Responses never
contain values, only `{ "NAME": { "hasValue": bool } }`.

envMappingIds.description: Reusable environment mapping IDs attached to this profile.

nativeToolPermissions.description: Native harness tool name -> allow|ask|deny (OpenCode permission map).

markdown.description: Markdown with relative links rewritten to documentation routes.

url.description: API route of the page, e.g. `/api/v1/docs/architecture/overview`.

EgressMode.description:
Requested network egress mode.

**Not yet enforced by the platform.** The value is validated and recorded on the
agent spec only; no ORBIT component restricts outbound traffic. Enforce egress at
the network layer (for example a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy).

EnvVarState.description: What a response says about a stored profile variable: never the value.

ExecutionStatus.description: Execution lifecycle. Terminal states are final and immutable.

HarnessCapabilities.description:
Capabilities a harness advertises. The UI and dispatch logic must branch on these,
never on a hardcoded harness name.

harnessManagedProviders.description: The harness owns its provider inventory and credentials (OpenCode Go, Claude Code).

supportsPlatformProviders.description: Harnesses that can consume a provider configured by ORBIT.

HarnessDescriptor.description: Static description of a harness family, exposed through `GET /api/v1/harnesses`.

status.description: `unknown` in Phase 0: harness health is reported by workers in a later phase.

HarnessKind.description:
Agent harness families ORBIT can orchestrate.

The enumeration is intentionally small and lives in the domain so that the API and
UI can reason about harnesses without depending on adapter crates. New harnesses can be
added here plus a registered `HarnessAdapter`; no other domain changes are required.

defaultHarness.description: Harness used when an execution/trigger does not select one.

config.description: Harness-specific configuration. Validated by the adapter, opaque to the core.

placement.description: Where the agent may execute. `auto` lets any matching worker claim it.

oneOf.description: What an apply would do (or did). Absent when the item cannot be applied.

id.description: Id of the created/updated resource. Only set after a real import.

warnings.description: Non-blocking notes: ignored fields, credentials to set, dropped secrets.

valid.description: True when every item can be (or was) applied.

activate.description: Activate a newly imported agent immediately.

constraints.description: Additional operator constraints, appended to the trusted instruction block.

system.description: Trusted system instructions. Always transported separately from untrusted input.

executionsPerDay.description: Signed claims spell it `executions_per_day` (ADR 0010); the API returns camelCase.

oneOf.description: Installation-wide usage; omitted for roles other than Owner and Admin.

availableFeatures.description: Signed flags backed by shipped functionality. This is what the API/UI advertises.

daysRemaining.description: Whole days until expiry; negative once the expiry date has passed.

features.description:
Raw signed flags. Reserved flags remain here because the verifier accepts them and
existing gates still read them; use [`LicenseStatus::available_features`] for display.

grace.description: True while inside the post-expiry grace window.

graceEndsAt.description:
End of the grace window. Set for signed licenses so the UI can show a positive
"grace ends in X days" countdown instead of negative expiry days.

tier.description: `community`, `enterprise`, … (the plan while the license is usable).

valid.description: False for community, invalid, or fully expired licenses.

LicenseUsage.description:
Counts are installation-wide (all organizations) because licenses are installed once
per ORBIT installation, not per organization. They are returned to Owners and Admins
only (#325).

docsUrl.description: Route of the embedded documentation index (authenticated).

params.description: Passthrough generation parameters for the selected provider.

NetworkPolicy.description:
Desired network egress policy for an agent.

**Recorded but not yet enforced by the platform.** Neither the worker nor any
harness adapter reads these values; enforce egress at the network layer (for
example a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy).

allowedHosts.description: Hostnames or `*.suffix` patterns. A bare `*` is rejected. Recorded but not yet enforced.

oneOf.description: Requested egress mode. Recorded but not yet enforced.

autoCreateTeams.description: Create missing access teams for mapped groups.

emailClaim.description: Claim used as the unique OIDC identity/email (default `email`).

groupRoles.description: IdP group/claim value -> ORBIT role name.

requireMappedGroup.description: Deny users whose groups match no role/team mapping.

requireVerifiedEmail.description:
Link an incoming identity to an existing user by email only when the token says
`email_verified: true` (a missing claim also blocks linking). This setting can
only turn the requirement on: it is already on unless
`ORBIT_OIDC_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL=false` turned it off (the default is on).

syncRoles.description: Re-evaluate the stored role on every login when a mapping matches.

OutputDeliveryView.description: One delivery of an output: whether the message arrived, and why not.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed. Never contains the webhook URL.

executionId.description: The run it reports on, only when the caller may see it.

nextAttemptAt.description: When a pending delivery is tried next.

responseStatus.description: HTTP status of the last attempt, when the destination answered.

status.description:
`pending` (waiting, or retrying after an error), `sending`, `succeeded`, `failed`
(refused, not retried), `dead` (retries used up) or `skipped` (output off or deleted).

botToken.description: Telegram bot token. Write-only; never returned, logged or published in events.

messageThreadId.description: Optional numeric Telegram forum topic id.

webhookUrl.description: Incoming webhook / target URL for webhook kinds. Write-only; never returned.

hasWebhook.description:
True when a webhook URL or Telegram bot token is stored. The value itself is never
returned.

oneOf.description:
The newest delivery, without run details. Only in list responses, and only once the
output has delivered (or tried to).

PlacementTarget.description:
Where an agent is allowed to execute. This is a routing constraint, not a guarantee
of process isolation; isolation depends on the worker's execution driver.

PortableDocument.description: The generic envelope. `spec` is validated against the typed spec of `kind`.

oneOf.description: Informational only: ignored on import. Credentials are set after import.

ProviderCompat.description: Explicit endpoint feature flags. "OpenAI-compatible" is not a guarantee.

ProviderKind.description:
Provider families. New kinds extend this enum plus a config struct; unrelated
modules are unaffected.

ResourceLimits.description: Limits enforced by the platform and honoured by harness isolation.

task.description: Pre-filled task for manual runs. Never used as system instructions.

intervalSeconds.description: Delay between monitor runs. Default 60 seconds, minimum 5.

canManageTeam.description: Whether the caller may change this team's membership.

orgVisibleCount.description:
Team-owned resources with organization visibility (everyone can see them when
strict team isolation is disabled).

resources.description: Visible resources relevant to this team, grouped by resource type.

roles.description: Member counts by team role. Decimal role names avoid colliding with reserved words.

effectiveAccess.description: Effective access for the calling principal: `view`, `use` and/or `manage`.

isOwnerTeam.description: Whether this team is the resource's owning team.

ownerName.description: Display name of the owning user, or `None` when the resource has no user owner.

ToolPolicyMatcher.description:
Fields a rule can match on. Every configured field must match (AND). An empty matcher
matches every tool call and is useful for a default `require_approval` policy.

capability.description: Glob against the connector capability, e.g. `issues.*`.

commandRegex.description:
Regular expression against shell commands (`command`, `cmd`). Best-effort, not a
sandbox; deny and require-approval rules match when no command can be extracted.

pathGlob.description:
Glob against path-like arguments (`path`, `file_path`, `paths`, …). Deny and
require-approval rules also match when no path can be extracted (fail closed).

tool.description: Glob against the tool name (`*` and `?` are wildcards).

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression, evaluated in `timezone` (UTC when omitted).

task.description:
What the agent is asked to do each time the schedule fires. Without it the
run gets a generic "perform your configured task" prompt.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name such as `Europe/Amsterdam`; defaults to UTC.

path.description: Where it was found, for example `spec.skills[1]`.

reference.description: The name/slug as written in the document.

oneOf.description: A new full definition; creates a new immutable version when the spec changed.

expectedVersion.description:
The agent version this edit started from. When given and the agent has a newer
version by now, the update is refused with 409 instead of overwriting it.

credential.description: Replacement credential. Omit to keep the current secret.

settings.description:
Partial or full OIDC settings. Fields that are absent keep their stored value.
Kept as raw JSON so "absent" can be told apart from "empty"; the schema is
still `OidcSettings`.

env.description:
Stored variable values. Never serialized: responses carry only names and a
`hasValue` flag (AGENTS.md rule 4). Read the field directly for the launcher
payload and for update merging.
